title: Bubbles' demand for runner-ups and the Sporting Life role
summary: Bubbles would ask Green if he had any runner-ups, and Green praises Bubbles' Sporting Life in Porgy and Bess, a favourite of Gershwin.

story.theme_name: Singers and the musicians who accompanied them

blocks.x: What sort of thing did John Bubbles say to you when he eventually saw you again and you would do something like the walking tap? What sort of thing would he say to you? I mean, would he say, 'Not good enough'?
He would say, 'You got any runner ups?'
Typical master -- one always had to do better and better.

He had such a -- well, he could do whatever he had a mind to do, because like (unintelligible) and he was some kind of a delinquent in the community and sporting life sent him back to his maker. He though he could outsing the (unintelligible) or something, you know. Well, he was the one -- I think he was the favorite of George Gershwin, you know, and that Sporting Life, you see.
